name: GuestPass
description: Send someone a temporary link to one movie, episode, season or series. They watch it without an account and without seeing the rest of your library. Injects its client script in memory, so it works on containers with a read-only or root-owned web root. GPL-3.0 fork of Franciskid/jellyfin-plugin-sharelinks.
overview: Expiring guest links for Jellyfin, no account needed.

versions.changelog: A logo for the plugin, shown in Jellyfin's plugin catalog and on the installed plugins page. Repository changes, no effect on the plugin itself: The release zip now carries logo.png next to the dll and meta.json, and the release workflow checks the zip holds exactly those three files instead of only rejecting known-bad names. logo.svg is the editable source of the logo.

For Jellyfin 12.2. Jellyfin 12 runs on .NET 10 and no longer loads plugins built for 10.11, so this release is rebuilt for it. Servers still on Jellyfin 10.11 should stay on 0.2.3, which remains in the catalog for them. Built for Jellyfin 12.2 and .NET 10 (targetAbi 12.2.0.0). The guest-user calls GuestPass makes through reflection were checked against Jellyfin 12.2: changing a password now takes a user id instead of a user object, which the existing id-based fallback already covers, and everything else is unchanged. Works alongside other plugins that add scripts to the web client. GuestPass used to answer the request for the web client's index.html on its own and never pass it on, which hid the scripts of every other plugin that injects into the same page, such as MeTube for Jellyfin. It now lets Jellyfin serve the page and adds its script to the response on the way out, so all of them load. The page is still never modified on disk, and browsers still cannot revalidate their way back to an unpatched copy. The client script now reports the right version (0.2.3 still said 0.2.2). Repository changes, no effect on the plugin itself: The release workflow reads the target framework and targetAbi from meta.json instead of hard-coding them, refuses to release when guestpass.js reports a different version, and fills the catalog changelog from this file instead of "See the GitHub release notes." Builds use the .NET 10 SDK, pinned through a new global.json.

Two fixes. GuestPass no longer appears on non-media menus such as the Users dashboard: the entry is only added after the server confirms the item is a movie, episode, series or season, instead of guessing from menu ids. Opening a share link no longer logs you out: if the browser already has a working sign-in for this server, that session is kept and the shared title just opens in it, instead of the guest session overwriting your login (which previously left you on a black page after the link was revoked). If you do get stuck on a black page from an older link, clear the site's storage or run localStorage.clear() in the console.

Hardening from a code review of 0.2.0. Deleting a link no longer removes its record when teardown failed, so a failed cleanup stays visible and is retried instead of silently orphaning a guest user or tag. Guest teardown now finds the guest user by its deterministic name as a last resort, closing a window where a crash or a delete racing a redemption could leave an enabled guest account behind. The guest session count is capped instead of unlimited, so repeated opens of a link cannot pile up sessions without bound. Corrected the context-menu detection to jellyfin-web's real action ids. No change to how you create, share or revoke links.

Links now work every time until they expire or are revoked, instead of being one-time use, and work on several devices at once. Adds a Delete action that revokes a link and removes its record, so revoked links no longer pile up. The GuestPass entry no longer appears on the Users dashboard menu, only on movies, episodes, series and seasons. Removes the stray French line on the dead-link page.

First GuestPass release. Fork of Franciskid/jellyfin-plugin-sharelinks with the on-disk index.html rewrite replaced by in-memory IStartupFilter injection, so the plugin works on containers whose web root is not writable. Adds an injection status panel, a switch to disable injection without uninstalling, and context-menu matching for non-English web clients including Dutch and German.
